provider: SURF Research Drive (Netherlands) — up to 5 TB free via NWO-funded Small Compute applications

free_tier.stated: Community Edition: 'Are you working at an institution without its own Research Drive environment? Then apply for access to Research Drive Community Edition here. You will receive up to 5 TB of storage space.' Institutional instances have their own (much larger) quotas set per institution.

egress.terms: Unmetered — SURF is the Dutch national e-infrastructure, no egress product exists.

tooling: Research Drive is ownCloud/Nextcloud-based, so the standard desktop sync client and WebDAV endpoints work; rclone's webdav backend applies. Not S3.
chaining: 5 TB per project via Small Compute, and the same application also unlocks 'max. 10TB project space storage' on Snellius, 'up to 200TB disk storage, 300TB tape storage' on Grid/Spider for data processing, and 'max. 50TB offline tape storage' — one NWO-funded application can therefore land 200+ TB of storage plus 5 TB of Research Drive.
limits_note: per-object-cap: not published for Research Drive; the SURF bundle page caps 'max. 10TB project space storage' on Snellius and 'up to 200TB disk storage' on Grid/Spider. request-rate: not published. Retention: tied to the project; SURF states data is retained for the project duration. Gate: 'researchers must have either a tenured appointment ... or a tenure track appointment at one of the research organisations listed' — a genuinely institution-gated, NWO-funded scheme.
reliability_note: servicedesk.surf.nl returns 401 to the reader and www.surf.nl intermittently 504s; the numbers here come from the live NWO page and a 2026-03-11 Wayback capture of the Research Drive page.

evidence.proved: 'Research Drive - via SURF max. 5TB or via institution', 'max. 50TB offline tape storage, if required max. 10TB project space storage', 'up to 200TB disk storage, 300TB tape storage', 'tenured appointment ... or a tenure track appointment'
